question: What is included in the service desk?
html:
The service desk is built around HELIX, which we are turning into a product-led service desk with a Tier-0 AI agent as the first line of support (Frontline growth plan). Our current context does not include a full service catalog, so the detailed scope below covers only what the growth plan names.

What the plan names

  • HELIX service desk. This is the core desk. Phase 1 (months 0-12) moves it to a product-led model (Frontline growth plan).
  • Tier-0 AI agent. It sits in front of human agents and handles requests before they become tickets. The plan expects this deflection to lift margin (est.).
  • Delivery base. Support is delivered nationally with a heavy offshore team in Goa, Hyderabad and Cape Town (Frontline public filings).

Add-ons planned in Phase 1

ComponentWhat it isSource
Tier-0 AI agentFirst-line automated support inside HELIXFrontline growth plan
Cyber-posture subscriptionRecurring security-posture service added to the deskFrontline growth plan
Legal-AI enablementHelp AM Law firms move Copilot from pilot to firm-wide useFrontline growth plan

The legal-AI offer targets a clear gap. ILTA finds 68% of firms have Copilot, but only 8% have deployed it firm-wide (Frontline growth plan).

What the context does not cover

  • Tier structure beyond Tier-0, such as Tier-1 to Tier-3 escalation
  • Hours of coverage, SLAs and response targets
  • Which applications are supported, for example document management, time entry or practice systems
  • Pricing model, whether per user, per seat or per ticket

A current service catalog, sample client contracts and HELIX ticket data by category would answer these. We would rather point to those sources than guess.

Expected financial effect

The KPI roadmap assumes margin rises from about 15.4% now to about 16.7% at month 12 (est.). It credits that rise to Tier-0 deflection and cyber attach (Frontline growth plan). These are assumptions built on analyst revenue and EBITDA estimates, not company disclosures (Frontline public filings).

With roughly $137M+ of equity and a $90M term loan behind the deal, EBITDA growth has to carry the return. A desk that deflects more tickets and adds recurring security revenue is the first place that growth shows up (est.).

Next actions

  • Pull the current HELIX service catalog and SLA schedule, so the full scope is documented rather than inferred.
  • Baseline ticket volume by category to size realistic Tier-0 deflection before the margin assumption is locked.
  • Define the cyber-posture subscription scope and test attach with a sample of AM Law clients.
  • Draft a legal-AI enablement offer aimed at firms that hold Copilot licences but have not deployed them firm-wide.
